headline: High data-leakage and compliance risk: RD-Agent’s broad API/key use can expose Plano’s logs/metrics if paired through shared outputs, while both agents’ broad egress increases cascading misuse risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, but both agents can exchange content through files or copied outputs: plano reads config.yaml and RD-Agent writes log/ and runs browsers/APIs. That makes manual or file-based prompt injection plausible, though not default. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented surfaces, not reproduced.
conditions: IF the operator copies RD-Agent outputs into plano prompts or config files
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared directory or log bundle
mitigations: Keep agents in separate directories
Disable copy-paste of untrusted agent output into prompts
Review any file passed from RD-Agent before plano consumes it
Use a one-way export format with explicit provenance labels

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles secrets and sensitive research data classes, while plano has broad network egress and OpenAI-compatible API calls. If they share a workspace or logs, RD-Agent material can flow into plano prompts and then to a third-party backend. Plano’s docs do not show local-only inference, so the leakage path is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF plano is given RD-Agent logs, traces, or secrets via a shared workspace
IF plano forwards those inputs to its OpenAI-compatible endpoint
mitigations: Do not place RD-Agent logs in plano-readable paths
Redact secrets before any handoff
Route plano to a local or private endpoint
Separate credentials and workspaces per agent
Add a manual review step before any cross-agent file transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and plano can call an OpenAI-compatible endpoint while RD-Agent can call multiple APIs including OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, and Kaggle. Even without filesystem write overlap, overlapping mutable external resources and API quotas can conflict. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same API keys or shared quota-bearing endpoints
IF both write to the same external project or dataset
mitigations: Use separate API keys per agent
Set per-agent rate limits
Avoid shared mutable datasets
Serialize writes to any shared external resource
Monitor quota and error spikes during parallel runs

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent is a research automation system with browser/API access, and plano is an AI gateway/router that can relay model outputs. If RD-Agent’s generated facts or traces are fed into plano without verification, errors can cascade into downstream decisions or routed responses. The profiles suggest the pathway but do not prove automatic trust, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF RD-Agent outputs are used as authoritative inputs to plano routing or responses
IF no human or programmatic verification step checks RD-Agent claims
mitigations: Require source citations before forwarding outputs
Add a verification step between agents
Limit plano to pass-through only for vetted content
Flag low-confidence RD-Agent outputs for review
Log provenance for every cross-agent claim

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles secrets and research/financial data classes and uses third-party APIs; plano also has broad egress and OpenAI-compatible calls. If regulated or confidential data from RD-Agent reaches plano, it can leave the controlled environment without a documented residency or retention boundary. Because the profiles show no compliance controls, uncertainty escalates this to high.
conditions: IF regulated, confidential, or customer data from RD-Agent is routed through plano
IF the destination API is outside the required residency or retention regime
mitigations: Block regulated data from cross-agent routing
Use a residency-approved endpoint only
Document retention and deletion rules for both agents
Separate environments for confidential and non-confidential workloads
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement on outbound requests
